summary: Only the remains of the Deacon tower are described, lying beside a portage at Brent in Algonquin Park.

facts.status_note: Only the remains are left, on the forest floor beside a portage.

access.note: Inside Algonquin Provincial Park; Brent is an access point to the park's interior.

visit.trail_note: Remains only, beside a portage; there is no standing tower to climb.

events.note: Shown on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map

evidence.supports: shown on 1963 Department of Lands and Forests tower map
evidence.quote: Appears on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963).

evidence.supports: Brent on Cedar Lake in northern Algonquin Park
evidence.quote: Brent is a community on Cedar Lake on the Petawawa River in northern Algonquin Provincial Park

evidence.supports: Deacon Township, unorganized south part of Nipissing District
evidence.quote: is located in geographic Deacon Township in the unorganized south part of Nipissing District in Northeastern Ontario

evidence.supports: began as a railway station on the Canadian Northern main line
evidence.quote: It was originally a station and divisional point on the transcontinental main line of the Canadian Northern Railway

evidence.supports: lumber companies operated at Brent in late 19th and early 20th century
evidence.quote: During the late 19th and early 20th century, a number of lumber companies operated at Brent.

evidence.supports: remains on forest floor beside the Pan Lake to Ghost Lake portage
evidence.quote: The remains of the old Brent fire tower lie on the forest floor adjacent to the portage from Pan Lake to Ghost Lake in Algonquin Park.

evidence.supports: Brent today: camp site with park services, access to park interior
evidence.quote: Brent today is essentially a recreational camp site with some park services and is an access point to the interior of Algonquin Park.

notes_for_editor: Identity inferred, not stated: firelookout.ca's Deacon record gives the location as Brent, Ontario, and mcelroy.ca calls the Brent tower by name, but no source ties the name Deacon to this tower in so many words. The brief had no local_unit; 'Nipissing District' comes from Wikipedia's 'unorganized south part of Nipissing District'. No readable source gives a build date, design, or staffing, so none is recorded. Firelookout coordinates 46.0625, -78.43806 were not checked against an independent point for Brent. The Algonquin Fire Tower Trail page (Sunday Creek, 45.583922, -78.359455) describes a different site and was not used. Two searches used; an Ontario Parks or Algonquin Park history source for the Brent tower's build and removal would be the next step.
